title: Basic operations and coefficient reduction
statement:
For the derived-complete
coefficient categories, reduction $\mathcal O_E\to A_{E,n}$ commutes
with derived pullback, tensor, ordinary direct image and compact-support
direct image on their stated bounded domains. Finite reduction
$A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ commutes with pullback, tensor and
compact-support direct image on the finite-Tor domains.
For $\mathcal O_E\to A_{E,n}$, internal Hom and evaluation commute
with reduction for arbitrary first variables on the stated integral
domains. Between finite quotient rings, the elementary comparison
proved here assumes that the first variable is
site-perfect; this includes
the coefficient dual of a perfect complex at a point.
For admissible
exceptional adjoints, use the coefficient comparisons required in
that admissibility hypothesis. The same operations and comparisons
commute with rationalization
and common-stage
scalar extension. All the displayed comparisons preserve the tensor
associativity maps, evaluations, units and counits used to construct
the projection and exchange transformations.

proof.text: Use the small pro-etale coefficient sites and operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and write $F_{A,B}=-\otimes_A^LB$ for coefficient extension. For finite $A\to B$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] applied to the identity topos gives $F_{A,B}(M\otimes_A^LN)\cong F_{A,B}M\otimes_B^LF_{A,B}N$. For pullback apply the same K-flat construction to the commuting square of coefficient ring maps on $X$ and $Y$: both $Lf_B^*F_{A,B}K$ and $F_{A,B}Lf_A^*K$ are represented by $B_X\otimes_{f^{-1}A_Y}f^{-1}P$ for a flat-term K-flat replacement $P$ of $K$. The derived tensor-pullback lemma ensures these pullbacks are K-flat, so these are comparisons of derived functors, not merely underived tensor expressions. The two routes through a threefold coefficient extension send $((x\otimes a)\otimes b)$ to $x\otimes ab$; the tensor comparison sends $(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes b)$ to $(x\otimes y)\otimes ab$. These formulas prove the associativity and unit identities and descend through quasi-isomorphisms. At integral level the operations are completed pullback and completed tensor, so one cannot simply omit completion: clauses (1) and (2) of [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] supply their canonical reduction isomorphisms. Their quotient-level maps are the same tensor formulas just written, so their associativity and units have those formulas after reduction as well.

For finite $A=A_{E,n}\to B=A_{E,m}$ let $K$ be site-perfect [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. The ringed-site duality theorem [lem-sfb-ringed-site-perfect-duality] gives $R\mathcal Hom_A(K,L)=K^\vee\otimes_A^L L$ for arbitrary $L$, with its evaluation-defined map, and makes $K^\vee$ perfect. Locally represent $K$ by a bounded complex $P$ of finite-projective sheaves. The canonical map $P^\vee\otimes_A B\to(P\otimes_A B)^\vee$ is a chain isomorphism: for $P^i=A^r$ it is the identity on $B^r$, and for a summand it is the restriction of that identity along the tensor of its splitting. Only finitely many degrees occur, and precomposition with the differential gives the same dual differential on both sides. Apply the tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and the duality theorem over $A$ and $B$ to obtain
$$F R\mathcal Hom_A(K,L)\cong F(K^\vee)\otimes_B^L FL\cong(FK)^\vee\otimes_B^L FL\cong R\mathcal Hom_B(FK,FL).$$
The local map is the transpose of reduced evaluation: on each term it sends $h\otimes b,p\otimes c$ to $h(p)\otimes bc$, with the same total-complex signs. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] this is the restriction of the global comparison; the local-isomorphism criterion of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-restriction], for the identity morphism, proves it invertible globally. No finite-Tor hypothesis on $L$ is used. The perfectness of the coefficient dual of a perfect point complex is also the duality theorem's first conclusion.

proof.text: For integral coefficients the first variable need not be perfect. The finite free resolution $[\mathcal O_E\xrightarrow{\varpi_E^n}\mathcal O_E]$ is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect]. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $\mathcal O_E$ is a principal ideal domain, hence Noetherian since every ideal is finitely generated. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] to obtain the actual resolution $[R\xrightarrow{\varpi_E^n}R]$ of $B=(A_{E,n})_W$ over $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$; ring-module perfectness alone would not identify these sheaves. The ambient comparison theorem [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction] now gives $R\mathcal Hom_R(K,L)\otimes_R^LB\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_B(K_n,L_n)$ for arbitrary $K,L$, and says that this very map is the transpose of reduced evaluation. It also gives completeness of the integral Hom when $L$ is complete. Restrict this ambient assertion to exactly those integral pairs for which the Hom belongs to the stated constructible category. In the two-term description, commuting Hom in the second variable with this finite cone accounts for the first isomorphism of the blueprint, and extension-restriction adjunction accounts for the second. The cited ambient theorem provides both assertions together with their specified evaluation normalization; no general finite-level Hom comparison is being inferred without the site-perfect hypothesis of step 2.

proof.text: For ordinary direct image apply [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula] to $P_n=(A_{E,n})_Y$, which is site-perfect over the completed coefficient sheaf by the two-term resolution in step 3. Its specified projection map is an isomorphism $(Rf_*K)\otimes^L P_n\to Rf_*K_n$, and the theorem gives its compatibility with quotient maps. [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] identifies ordinary direct image of a complete object with the derived limit of its finite-level images, including the completion map and the Roos transition operator $1-s$. Thus it identifies this object with the integral direct image actually defined in [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. On the stated finite-type bounded constructible domains, [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible] explicitly says that the comparison from that definition is an isomorphism and that the images are bounded constructible, with a uniform cohomological bound independent of $n$. These are complementary assertions: the projection formula fixes the map, the limit theorem fixes the completed realization, and the constructibility theorem fixes its bounded domain.

proof.text: Choose the single compactification $f=pj$ used in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], with $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ quasi-compact open and $p$ proper. The compactification schemes are finite type over the base field: p is proper, hence finite type, and finite-type morphisms compose by adjoining the two finite sets of algebra generators. A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes the compactification schemes Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] makes all their opens and intersections quasi-compact. This verifies the quasi-compactness of j and the constructibility of the strata used in step 6. Work over the completed coefficient sheaf on $\overline X$ and its restriction to $X$. Extension by zero $J=j_!$ is exact and left adjoint to restriction by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]; the coefficient restrictions are canonical by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. The tensor identity [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor], using the open-slice identification [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], gives $J(Q\otimes j^{-1}C)\cong JQ\otimes C$. The same formula holds for total tensor complexes because J preserves their direct sums by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. For a K-flat representative $Q$ of $K$ supplied by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], $JQ$ is K-flat: for acyclic $C$, exact restriction makes $j^{-1}C$ acyclic by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation], then $Q\otimes j^{-1}C$ is acyclic and exact $J$ preserves that. Applying the tensor identity to each finite coefficient quotient therefore gives $(JK)_n\cong j_!K_n$. It respects the quotient maps because on these representatives the transition is $1\otimes(A_{E,n+1}\to A_{E,n})$ on both sides. It respects the maps from $JK$ because both send a local section to its tensor with $1$.

The completeness assertion of [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison], applied to the identity cartesian square for this quasi-compact $j$, says that $JK$ is derived complete. Moreover $JK$ is integral constructible: by step 5 its reductions are $j_!K_n$; exactness of $j_!$ identifies their cohomology with extension by zero of the cohomology of $K_n$. Add the closed complement to any finite stratification witnessing finite-torsion constructibility [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. On the old strata the sheaf is unchanged and on the new stratum it is zero; all these strata are constructible in the Noetherian compactification. The same uniform cohomological interval works since $j_!$ is exact. This verifies all the conditions in [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Step 4 applied to $p$ and $JK$ now identifies the reductions of $Rp_*JK$ with $Rp_{*,n}j_!K_n=Rf_{!,n}K_n$. The integral compact-support definition is the derived limit of precisely this tower. The transition identifications in step 5 and the tower naturality in [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] identify its comparison with the reduction of $Rp_*JK$, not just with an abstract isomorphism between these objects. This proves $(Rf_!K)_n\cong Rf_{!,n}K_n$.

proof.text: For $1\leq m\leq n$, the finite-level compact-support comparison is exactly [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]: its hypotheses require the separated finite-type morphism in the finite-field datum and a bounded constructible finite-Tor input. Its statement includes successive reduction, pullback and the counits defining the projection map, so this citation proves those clauses for the specified comparison. For exceptional right adjoints the item makes a conditional assertion only: in [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility], admissibility at $\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ explicitly requires the finite-reduction and scalar-extension maps of the right adjoints to be isomorphisms. Invoke precisely that requirement whenever such an adjoint is used. Finite-stage admissibility alone has no coefficient-isomorphism clause and is not being used to deduce one. The units and counits mentioned below are those of the chosen adjunctions; no ambient right adjoint is asserted for a morphism for which the admissibility conditions fail.

source.place: paragraph 2, finite compact-support change and admissibility qualification

proof.text: For finite $E\subset L$, use the completed pullback/tensor/Hom comparisons and tower laws of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. By [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], scalar extension is ordinary tensor by $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,W}$, finite free over $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$. Step 5's coefficient inverse-image identifications give compatible ringed squares. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction] with terminal index category: finite freeness implies flatness, and its restriction/direct-image comparison identifies the coefficient target, including adjuncts. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula] with the site-perfect object $S_Y$ to get the direct-image scalar isomorphism. Naturality for multiplication by sections makes it $S_Y$-linear. The evaluation-defined scalar-Hom isomorphism for arbitrary variables is [lem-sf-ringed-finite-free-hom-base-change]; its finite-free hypothesis was just verified, and its transpose is exactly scalar extension of evaluation. For compact support combine the proper-factor comparison with step 5's open tensor comparison. In the strict-tower triangle of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], finite-free tensor commutes with derived products and cones: in a basis it is a finite sum of identity functors. The scalar-comparison lemma identifies this realization with the defined integral scalar extension. For $R\to S\to T$, the tensor and Hom maps send $x\otimes s\otimes t$ to $x\otimes st$ and $h\otimes s\otimes t$ to $(p\otimes u\mapsto h(p)\otimes stu)$. Direct-image composites are mates of the same pullback map, hence equal by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]; the product-cone construction gives compact-support equality. With $S=R$ all formulas are identities.

proof.text: Rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] leaves objects unchanged and replaces each integral Hom group by its tensor product with $E$. The operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] are defined there by linear extension of the integral operations, and direct image and compact support are likewise rationalized in [def-weil-derived-direct-image, def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. A commuting integral comparison square remains commuting after this linear extension: expand a morphism as a finite sum of $u_i\otimes a_i$, apply linearity to each summand, and use the integral square for $u_i$. Inverses remain inverses. At the algebraic-closure stage [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], represent the finitely many objects and maps of a comparison diagram over one common finite extension. The integral scalar comparisons of step 8 and the exact transition functors [lem-weil-scalar-extension-exact-triangulated] give the diagrams at that stage. After enlarging the field their diagrams agree by the identity and tower laws of step 8. Thus they give well-defined comparison maps on the common-stage category, and any equality follows from the equality at that common stage. This is transport in the prescribed localized and common-stage categories, not an identification with discrete constant-field sheaf categories.

Write $F_X,F_Y$ for coefficient extension, $L_A\dashv R_A$, $L_B\dashv R_B$ for pullback/direct image, and $a:L_BF_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}F_XL_A$ for step 1. Define $b:F_YR_A\to R_BF_X$ by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Its transpose gives the counit equation
$$\varepsilon_B F_X\circ L_B b=F_X\varepsilon_A\circ aR_A.$$
The inverse-mate formula, naturality and the two triangle identities give
$$R_Ba\circ\eta_B F_Y=bL_A\circ F_Y\eta_A.$$
The projection comparison is this transpose [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], with step 1's tensor constraint. The finite compact-support counit equation is included in [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]. For Hom the equation is
$$\operatorname{ev}_B\circ(c\otimes1)=F(\operatorname{ev}_A)\circ\mu^{-1},$$
with $\mu$ the tensor comparison. Step 2's dual evaluation calculation, [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction], and [lem-sf-ringed-finite-free-hom-base-change] give this equation for finite site-perfect, integral and scalar comparisons respectively. Applying the adjunction bijection shows compatibility with tensor-Hom transposes. Thus transposing either route in a projection or exchange square gives the same composite of evaluation, reassociation and counit. The displayed unit equation handles units. For successive coefficient changes both transposes have the same tensor formula, so injectivity of the adjunction bijection gives equality. Exceptional comparisons use their mates and the explicit admissibility isomorphism assumption of step 7; invertibility is not inferred merely by taking a mate. Step 9 carries these equations to rational and common-stage coefficients. These are equalities of the specified maps.

split_report.summary: Audited the unchanged imported statement against current main-20261015, searched both read-only Lean sources and Mathlib, and expanded the three source proof paragraphs into ten steps using existing nodes only. Replaced definition-only justifications by explicit completed-operation, Hom-model, quotient-sheaf, direct-image and finite-free scalar tools; separated bounded-domain checks from existence of ambient comparisons; and displayed evaluation and both mate identities. No new node, attachment or statement correction. The resumed audit removes an unnecessary finite-Tor condition on the finite-level Hom second variable by an explicit finite-filtration argument. Second reading specifies the finite filtration and local sheaf lifting in step 2, and adds the finite-free K-injective Hom calculation and mate tower equations in step 8 to justify scalar evaluation normalization and the maps used in step 9. Repair reading on 2026-10-17 replaces the long step-2 perfect-Hom argument, the step-8 finite-free Hom and restriction arguments by existing ringed-site lemmas, and abbreviates the mate calculation. The statement and all maintainer metadata are unchanged; this is a stage-1 delivery, not the stage-2 Lean delivery requested in the mismatched return.
